verdict.rationale: Context.dev's own docs say it scrapes pages and crawls sites into Markdown for AI agents, and its llms.txt describes the same Markdown output. Browser actions (click, wait, scroll before scraping) and page rendering for screenshots show it handles rendering for the user. Community questions about proxies are skepticism, not a documented failure, so they do not create a dispute. missing for 10: documented handling of anti-bot blocking or proxies, detail on how the Markdown is cleaned of page boilerplate, independent hands-on corroboration of output quality.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can get clean LLM-ready text directly instead of dealing with blocking, rendering, and messy HTML myself

citations.quote: Scrape websites into Markdown, crawl linked pages, and extract JSON for AI agents and applications.
Scrape a page into Markdown, HTML, a screenshot, images, or CSS-selected fields in one request.
Click, wait, or scroll before scraping or extracting a page, then check which interactions succeeded.
Crawl a small website section and return page Markdown in one response, with a maximum of 500 pages.
